# Odhisokathā (Kv 1.4)

**ID:** Kv 1.4
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Odhisokathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Odhisokathā* (Kv 1.4) is the fourth discourse in the first chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The controversy examined in this text concerns whether defilements (*kilesa*) are abandoned piecemeal or segment by segment (*odhiso odhiso*, *ekadesena ekadesena*) [Bareau 1955]. Opponents maintain that stream-enterers (*sotāpanna*) and other noble disciples abandon defilements progressively, one part after another, through distinct clear realizations (*nānābhisamayavasena*) when seeing the Noble Truth of suffering and the subsequent truths [Bareau 1955]. Against this, the Theravādin position argues that defilements are not put away piece by piece (*odhiso*); if corruptions were removed incrementally, a practitioner could be partly endowed with one of the fruits of recluseship (*sāmaññaphala*), which conflicts with the teachings of the Buddha [Aung & Rhys Davids 1915; Bareau 1955].

  DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan scholastic treatises, including Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, and Vimalamitra's *Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti* [DharmaNexus].
